A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SEELE framework, task inversion technique, and ReS dataset. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and duplicated material.

before.justification: V2 reports original ReS experiments and a 100-survey user study in Table 1, inpainting/outpainting results in Table 2, and qualitative experiments and ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds reproduced harmonization results, additional removal/completion metrics in Table 3, and illustrated failure cases.

M1.justification: The generative algorithm, task-specific masks, training objectives, and LoRA switching remain unchanged. A limited output-processing change is reported: v2 Section 14 only plans logo marking, whereas v3's Broader Impact Statement states that generated images receive watermarks.

E1.justification: Both versions cover ReS, MSCOCO, iHarmony4, Places2, and Flickr-Scenery, with the same repositioning, removal, completion, harmonization, inpainting, and outpainting tasks. The new quantitative harmonization comparison uses data and task coverage already represented in v2.

E2.justification: Table 3(a) newly evaluates DucoNet against SEELE for harmonization. Tables 1–2 retain their comparator sets, including the existing LoRA variant. The newly cited drag-based editing methods are discussed rather than experimentally compared.

E3.justification: The added harmonization comparison evaluates 512×512 outputs using PSNR and MSE, explicitly separating reproduced results from DucoNet's reported 256×256 results. Table 3(b) adds PSNR and SSIM to the removal/completion comparison. Existing training budgets, dataset splits, and the 100-survey design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 9 adds concrete failures involving unnatural shadows, incorrect depth, and erroneous cat expansion. Table 3 extends quantitative analysis of LoRA adaptation and harmonization model choice. The earlier prompt, harmonization-component, and preprocessing/postprocessing ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed specifications, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V3's additional results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Every numerical entry in Tables 1–2 is unchanged. New Table 3(a) reports PSNR/MSE of 31.88/78.74 for SEELE and 31.55/197.38 for reproduced DucoNet at 512×512. Table 3(b) adds PSNR/SSIM results for existing variants, and Figure 9 adds qualitative failure outcomes.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(2) and the appendix's LoRA integration algebra retain their mathematical content. Writing L(z) and explaining embedding dimensions clarify existing mathematics; no new assumptions, derivations, proofs, or formal results are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims: defining subject repositioning, addressing its generative subtasks through one diffusion backbone and task inversion, and introducing ReS. Additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V3 adds a resolution-generalization explanation for DucoNet's weaker 512×512 results and refines the existing LoRA overfitting argument in terms of preserving U-Net generalization. The failure taxonomy and limitations concerning manual masks and open-vocabulary amodal completion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 removes the Gradio UI documentation and ReS's stated native resolution of 4032×3024. It adds the CFFF computing-platform disclosure and explicitly states code availability. The appendix retains the optimizer, learning rate, batch size, training steps, GPU configuration, prompt size, and LoRA integration details.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds a focused discussion of DragGAN, DragDiffusion, and related drag-based methods, distinguishing subject completion and preservation of unchanged regions. DucoNet is newly cited for the harmonization comparison; the Gradio reference disappears with the UI section.

P1.justification: Section 3.1 expands the explanation of learned task prompts, their embedding interface, and their distinction from user inputs. Most narrative and main-section ordering remain intact. V3 consolidates the appendix into A.1–A.6, moves the impact statement before references, and updates author, affiliation, and citation formatting.

P2.justification: The journal layout substantially widens the text area and enlarges and reflows visual material throughout both main text and appendix. V3 rearranges Figure 4, adds Table 3 and failure Figure 9, and removes v2's duplicate displays in Figures 9 and 11 and the UI screenshot in Figure 15.

improvement.justification: Clearer task-prompt explanations in Section 3.1, additional comparisons in Table 3, and explicit failures in Figure 9 improve the paper's assessability. The drag-based related-work discussion also strengthens context. These limited gains outweigh the loss of some UI and dataset documentation; the central generative method and existing benchmark findings remain stable.
